correctness.rationale: The explicit dual-color conjugacy yields majority with tie-flip. For odd n and proper matching deletion at even n, count-based finite update paths from every state reach a polar absorber. At the even-size full-deletion endpoint every flip strictly raises cut weight, and a complete local-inequality classification gives exactly two polar absorbers plus binomial(n,n/2) balanced matched-pair absorbers. The two independent scripts prove the exact finite claims in their stated ranges: 22 state-transition graphs (36,352 configurations) and 39 independent stable-state censuses (757,248 configurations). Those experiments are supplementary to the all-size constructive proof.

value.rationale: The graph family interpolates canonically between complete bipartite and crown graphs. Adding a single edge to a dense network sharply removes exponentially many permanently frozen half-optimal cuts, a dimension-free final-edge stability transition. The statement gives both the all-parameter complete recurrent-class classification and an exact limiting entropy/price-of-anarchy comparison. This is a motivated structural result in local anti-coordination dynamics, not an arbitrary finite table or an unexplained invariant.
